91	## Exceptions Summary
92	
93	Three conditions relax the HIGH-confidence requirements introduced into Criteria 3 and 5.
94	This section is a navigation aid, listing them together for quick reference; where its
95	wording differs from the per-criterion clause, the per-criterion clause governs.
96	
97	**(a) Unreachable source** — Criterion 3. A ground truth cites a source the Phase 3
98	verification step could not open; the Phase 3 failure record naming which source and why
99	unreachable is the satisfying evidence; the ground truth may feed only MEDIUM or LOW chains.
100	
101	**(b) Speculative chain** — Criterion 5. A chain is explicitly marked speculative and the
102	analysis states the claim it supports is not load-bearing; the mark plus that statement is
103	the satisfying evidence; the chain may remain MEDIUM. Its confidence line still gives each of
104	its own downgrade causes what would remove it or an explicit account of why no available
105	evidence settles it, because the mark is not a no-path reason. A speculative chain cited on
106	another chain's head is load-bearing and no longer qualifies. A speculative chain with no
107	verification path is therefore not cited on another chain's head; it stays speculative or
108	moves to Abandoned Reasoning.
109	
110	**(c) Absent-fails derivation** — Criterion 5. A chain establishes that a conclusion does not
111	follow from an assumption shown to be false; the named false assumption is the satisfying
112	evidence; the chain may remain MEDIUM.
113	
114	An exception is claimed, not assumed: an analysis relying on one names it in the relevant
115	verdict block and cites the required evidence; an unclaimed exception is not applied on the
116	analysis's behalf.

120	## Scoring Model
121	
122	Score each of the 6 criteria using this shared 4-level scale, applied uniformly across all criteria
123	(highest to lowest):
124	
125	- **Rigorous** — the criterion's named artifact is present, structurally complete, and every
126	  entry meets the observable descriptor for this level: all required fields are populated with
127	  non-generic content, all required relationships are explicit,
128	  and every observable structural test in this criterion's Rigorous descriptor returns pass.
129	
130	- **Sound** — the criterion's named artifact is present and mostly meets the Rigorous descriptor,
131	  but one or more entries fall short in a specific, identifiable way: a field is generic or vague
132	  rather than empty, a relationship is implicit rather than absent, or one entry departs from the
133	  prescribed form without invalidating the rest.
134	
135	- **Hand-wavy** — the criterion's named artifact is present but fails the Rigorous descriptor in
136	  a pattern rather than an isolated entry: multiple fields are generic or empty, the artifact's
137	  prescribed structure is not followed, or the section uses the honest-depth escape valve with a
138	  reason that could be copy-pasted to any analysis without modification.
139	
140	- **Absent** — the criterion's named artifact is missing entirely, or the section exists but
141	  contains no content that could be scored against the artifact's descriptor (the section heading
142	  appears with nothing substantive below it).
143	
144	**Rank order (explicit):** Rigorous > Sound > Hand-wavy > Absent.
145	
146	**Gate:** Any criterion scored **Absent** fails the entire analysis — it must be revised and
147	re-scored, bounded to at most one re-perception pass per analysis, per "How to Apply This
148	Gate" above. If the criterion still scores Absent after that single pass, it is presented as
149	an unresolved gap with a stated confidence caveat instead of being withheld, regardless of how
150	all other criteria score.
151	
152	**Hand-wavy cap:** Two or more criteria scored **Hand-wavy** also fails the entire analysis —
153	the same bound applies: revise and re-score once, per "How to Apply This Gate" above. One
154	criterion at Hand-wavy is tolerated (one isolated weaker section does not indicate a systemic
155	quality problem); two or more at Hand-wavy indicates a pattern of shallow reasoning that the
156	gate alone cannot catch, because no single criterion has reached the gate-fail level. If two or
157	more criteria still score Hand-wavy after that single pass, the cap breach is presented as an
158	unresolved gap with a stated confidence caveat instead of being withheld.
159	
160	**Pass:** No criterion scores Absent, and at most one criterion scores Hand-wavy.
161	(Equivalently: every criterion is Sound or above, except at most one may be Hand-wavy.)
162	
163	**Escape-valve scoring (global rule, applies to every criterion):** Any section that
164	legitimately uses the honest-depth escape valve (`Nothing material here — [reason]`) is
165	scored **Rigorous** if the stated reason is specific to this analysis — it names a property
166	of this problem that makes the section's content unnecessary — and **Hand-wavy** if the
167	reason is generic or copy-pasteable to any analysis. A properly-used escape valve is
168	**never** scored Absent solely for using the escape valve: the per-criterion Absent
169	descriptors below apply to a section that is missing, empty, or filled with non-scoreable
170	content, not to a section that is honestly and specifically marked as having no material
171	content.
172	
173	**Load-bearing chain (definition):** A derivation chain is *load-bearing* if a claim in
174	the Conclusion section (output section 6) depends on it — i.e., the chain produces, or is
175	cited as support for, a conclusion the analysis actually presents. A chain that reaches
176	only an intermediate result no conclusion rests on is not load-bearing. (This is the
177	narrower scoring sense of the phrase `SKILL.md` uses informally as "load-bearing for a
178	high-stakes conclusion.")

182	## Verdict Block Format
183	
184	The six verdict blocks are emitted together under the single top-level heading
185	`## Self-Audit Gate (process output)`, one `##` heading holding all six in criterion order —
186	the same placement the adversarial pass record and the self-audit scan prescribe for themselves.
187	They are one artifact, not six; nesting them beneath another section's heading makes them a
188	subsection of something they do not belong to, and a reader or a check keyed to that heading
189	must find it in the same structural position on every run.
190	
191	Each of the 6 criteria requires exactly one verdict block. Use the standard form when the
192	analysis section exists and contains scoreable content:
193	
194	```text
195	**Criterion N: [Criterion Name]**
196	Quoted span: "[Direct quote of the specific text that most directly determines the band assigned — from the analysis being scored, or, per the admission below, from the self-audit scan for Criteria 4 and 6 or the Assumption Audit scan for Criterion 2, each emitted as process output for this analysis.]"
197	Band: [**Rigorous** / **Sound** / **Hand-wavy** / **Absent**]
198	Justification: [One sentence tying the quoted span to the observable descriptor for
199	that band — name the specific structural property present or absent.]
200	```
201	
202	The self-audit scan and the Assumption Audit scan are not output sections, and they are the only artifacts outside the six-section analysis a verdict block may quote: the self-audit scan for Criteria 4 and 6, and the Assumption Audit scan for Criterion 2. Every other criterion quotes the analysis text itself, and the §6→§4 closure ledger is admitted nowhere — it is a drafting artifact that describes a document other than the one being scored.
203	
204	Use the gap-citation form when the criterion scores Absent because the section or named
205	artifact is missing or empty — in that case there is no span to quote, and the documented
206	absence is the evidence:
207	
208	```text
209	**Criterion N: [Criterion Name]**
210	Gap: [Name what is missing and where it should have appeared — e.g., "No Derivation
211	Chains section exists; chains of the form 'GT-N + GT-M → [intermediate] → [conclusion]'
212	should appear in section 4 (Derivation Chains) for each conclusion stated in section 6
213	(Conclusion)."]
214	Band: Absent
215	Justification: [One sentence: the absence itself is the structural failure that triggers
216	the gate — the criterion cannot be scored against a non-existent artifact.]
217	```
218	
219	Verdict blocks (not a consolidated table) are required because each block contains a quoted
220	span or a gap citation. Without that span, the evidence-quoting requirement cannot be audited:
221	a summary table of band labels can be produced by asserting compliance, but a verdict block
222	containing a quote that contradicts its claimed band creates a contradiction that cannot be
223	sustained.

227	## Criteria
228	
229	Apply all six criteria in the order listed. Criteria 1-5 follow the order of the
230	six-section output format — the same chain-of-artifacts sequence the analysis itself
231	follows — so that a scoring pass moves through the analysis in the order it was produced;
232	Criterion 6 is a whole-document cross-section check applied last.
233	
234	### Criterion 1: Identify Essence
235	
236	Scores the **Essence Statement** — the single sentence naming the core problem followed by
237	a short list of success criteria — in the Problem Essence section (output section 1).
238	
239	- **Rigorous** — the Essence Statement is a single sentence that names the core question or
240	  decision (not a symptom, not the triggering event, not a restatement of the user's prompt);
241	  each success criterion contains a pass/fail structural test — a verb + subject + outcome
242	  triplet where the outcome is a property of the Conclusion section — so that a reviewer
243	  applies each criterion by scanning the Conclusion section without analyst interpretation;
244	  the statement is specific enough that it appears nowhere in an analysis of a different but
245	  related problem without modification (it names a property unique to this problem, not a
246	  generic template phrase).
247	  If this section uses the honest-depth escape valve (`Nothing material here — [reason]`), the
248	  stated reason is specific to this analysis's problem — it names a property of the problem
249	  that makes an Essence Statement unnecessary or redundant, and that reason appears in no
250	  other analysis without alteration.
251	
252	- **Sound** — the Essence Statement exists and names a question, but the success criteria are
253	  vague or stated in terms that cannot be verified against the conclusion without further
254	  clarification (e.g., "the solution should be good," "the approach should be appropriate").
255	
256	- **Hand-wavy** — the Essence Statement exists but names a symptom, a triggering event, or a
257	  restatement of the user's prompt rather than the underlying question; OR the success criteria
258	  are absent while the Essence Statement itself is present; OR the section uses the honest-depth
259	  escape valve with a reason that is generic and would apply equally to any analysis (e.g.,
260	  "no essence was needed").
261	
262	- **Absent** — no Essence Statement is present (the Problem Essence section is empty, contains
263	  only a restatement of the original prompt with no analytical distillation, or the section
264	  heading appears with nothing below it).
265	  This verdict routes back to Phase 1 to re-frame the Essence Statement — or, when the cause is an input that was never supplied, to re-opening input under the Input Contract — rather than an in-place rewrite of output section 1; the route is bounded by the same rule described under `SKILL.md`'s "Before presenting conclusions" section.
266	
267	### Criterion 2: Challenge Assumptions
268	
269	Scores the **Classified Assumptions Table** — a table with columns Assumption, Type, Treatment,
270	Verdict, Verification — in the Assumptions Table section (output section 2). Folds in:
271	four-type classification quality and unverified-flag discipline (D-07).
272	
273	- **Rigorous** — every row in the Assumptions Table has a Type value drawn from exactly the
274	  four-type scheme (physical law / current constraint / convention / untested belief); the
275	  Treatment cell uses the vocabulary of the prescribed treatment for that type; the Verdict
276	  cell records Accept, Challenge, or Discard as a leading token followed by an em-dash and a
277	  specific justification — not the bare token alone; the Verification cell cites a specific
278	  source or names what verification confirms the assumption — not "unclear" or "possibly true";
279	  at least one assumption has been challenged (not merely labelled Accept); if any assumption
280	  is used in a derivation chain despite being unverified, the Verification cell reads
281	  "unverified — flagged"; the Assumption Audit performed at the end of Phase 4 (`SKILL.md`,
282	  "End-of-phase Assumption Audit") visited every named derivation chain step in section 4 and
283	  surfaced any assumption not already in the Assumptions Table, recording it there; the
284	  Assumption Audit artifact produced before scoring (per "How to Apply This Gate") confirms
285	  this scan was exhaustive over named derivation chain steps, not an open-ended survey of the
286	  universe of conceivable assumptions.
287	
288	- **Sound** — the table exists with populated rows, but one or more rows have generic entries:
289	  the Verification cell reads "unclear" or "unsure" without specifics, OR the Treatment
290	  cell records a treatment that does not match the prescribed treatment for the row's Type,
291	  OR one assumption that is used in a chain despite being unverified lacks the
292	  "unverified — flagged" notation.
293	
294	- **Hand-wavy** — the table exists but uses Type values outside the four-type scheme (e.g.,
295	  "general assumption," "business constraint," freeform labels); OR multiple rows have empty
296	  Verdict or Verification cells; OR every assumption is labelled Accept with no challenge
297	  attempted and no evidence cited for any verdict.
298	
299	- **Absent** — no Assumptions Table is present; OR the table exists but every row's Type
300	  cell is empty, freeform (no mapping to the four-type scheme), or missing — making the
301	  table a list of undifferentiated claims rather than a classified set.
302	
303	### Criterion 3: Establish Ground Truths
304	
305	Scores the **Ground Truths list** — a numbered list of verified facts with stable GT-IDs,
306	source citations, and a provenance label, with unverified and delegate-reported entries marked
307	with the `GT-N?` suffix — in the Ground Truths section (output section 3).
308	
309	**Provenance check (apply before banding).** A citation being present is not verification. For
310	each unsuffixed ground truth, ask whether the analysis read the asserted figure in the cited
311	source — `read-at-source` — or merely received it from a sub-agent, search result, or summary
312	without opening the citation (`reported-by-delegate`, which requires the `?`). Score against
313	what the analysis did, not against how well-formed the citation looks.
314	
315	- **Rigorous** — every GT-item carries a stable identifier (GT-1, GT-2, etc.) that matches
316	  the identifiers referenced in the Derivation Chains section; every verified GT has a source
317	  citation that is more specific than "common knowledge" or "known fact"; every GT carries a
318	  provenance label; every unverified or delegate-reported GT is marked with the `?` suffix;
319	  the `?`-marked GTs are **enumerated by ID** and that enumeration matches the suffixed entries
320	  in the Ground Truths list when checked against it; every unsuffixed GT feeding a
321	  HIGH-confidence chain names its read-at-source location; no assumption that was discarded in
322	  Phase 2 (Verdict: Discard) appears in this list. Every unsuffixed GT whose cited source is
323	  reachable feeds at least one HIGH-confidence chain EXCEPT: the Phase 3 failure record names
324	  the source as unreachable, in which case the GT may feed only MEDIUM or LOW chains, evidenced
325	  by that record naming which source and why unreachable.
326	
327	  **Check the enumeration, do not quote it.** Quoting the analysis's own provenance summary as
328	  the satisfying span does not discharge this criterion — that verifies a summary was written,
329	  not that it is correct. Read the Ground Truths list, collect the IDs actually carrying `?`,
330	  and compare against the enumeration. Cite the comparison as the satisfying span (*"enumerated
331	  GT-2, GT-5, GT-9, GT-14; list carries `?` on exactly those four"*). Where a stated count and
332	  its enumeration disagree, the enumeration governs and the mismatched count is itself a defect.
333	
334	  **Reachability is decided by the Phase 3 record, not re-decided here.** A source is reachable
335	  when the Phase 3 verification step opened it, and unreachable when the Phase 3 failure record
336	  names it with a specific reason; the analyst reads the record and does not re-argue
337	  reachability per ground truth. This requirement is not satisfied by a ground truth that feeds
338	  no chain at all — a GT no derivation chain consumes is already a Criterion 4 defect, and the
339	  requirement presupposes at least one load-bearing chain consumes the GT. A single unsuffixed
340	  GT whose reachable source feeds only MEDIUM or LOW chains bands this criterion Sound; the same
341	  shortfall across multiple GTs bands it Hand-wavy.
342	
343	- **Sound** — GT-IDs are present and stable, but one or more verified GTs cite "common
344	  knowledge," "known fact," or no source at all; OR provenance labels are missing though the
345	  `?` suffixes themselves are correctly applied; OR one unread GT (unverified or
346	  delegate-reported) is used without the `?` suffix **and it feeds only MEDIUM or LOW
347	  confidence chains**; OR the `?`-marked GTs are summarized by a bare count rather than
348	  enumerated, though the suffixes in the list are themselves correct.
349	
350	  An enumeration that **disagrees with the list** does not band here — it bands **Hand-wavy**.
351	  A count that merely accompanies a correct enumeration and disagrees with it is a defect but
352	  bands Sound, since the enumeration governs and remains checkable.
353	
354	- **Hand-wavy** — GT-IDs are present but they are not stable (the same ID is used for
355	  different facts at different points in the document, or IDs are renumbered between sections);
356	  OR the list includes an assumption that was assigned a Discard verdict in Phase 2; OR
357	  multiple unread GTs are used in chains without the `?` suffix; OR **the `?` enumeration
358	  disagrees with the Ground Truths list** — an enumeration that omits a suffixed GT understates
359	  the analysis's unverified inputs in the direction that flatters it, and unlike a bare count it
360	  was checkable, so a mismatch is a stronger failure than never enumerating at all; OR **any
361	  unsuffixed GT feeds a HIGH-confidence chain without naming a read-at-source location** — a
362	  HIGH-confidence conclusion resting on a figure nobody read is the failure this criterion
363	  exists to catch, and a single instance is enough to land here.
364	
365	  **Fix — acquire before you downgrade.** Branch one, preferred: acquire the evidence — open
366	  the cited source, per the Phase 3 verification step, and let the read move the provenance
367	  label. Branch two: downgrade the confidence — carry the `?` and drop the chain from HIGH,
368	  taken only when the source cannot be opened or opens without containing the asserted figure or wording. The preference, explicitly: acquisition is preferred when the source is reachable, because a gate whose only available Fix weakens the output resolves every failure toward less claim rather than more evidence. The unreachable case is not a free pass — the downgrade branch still requires the Phase 3 failure record, which source and why unreachable, or `citation does not support the claim`, so a reader can tell a downgrade from a skipped attempt.
369	
370	- **Absent** — no GT-IDs are assigned to any fact in the Ground Truths section; OR the Ground
371	  Truths section lists claims without distinguishing verified from unverified (no `?` suffix
372	  appears anywhere, no citations appear anywhere, and the list is undifferentiated); OR the
373	  section is absent or empty.
374	
375	### Criterion 4: Reason Upward
376	
377	Scores **both** the **Derivation Chains** (output section 4) — one chain per conclusion,
378	formatted as `GT-N + GT-M → [intermediate claim] → [conclusion]` with at least one
379	intermediate step — **and** the **Abandoned Reasoning** section (output section 5).
380	Both sections are in scope for this criterion. Quoted span: where the band is determined by chain form or chain dependency, it must be drawn from the self-audit scan's chain-form table row or rows that determine the band, not from the Derivation Chains prose directly. Where the band is determined by the Abandoned Reasoning section, the no-analogies-as-direct-evidence ban, a missing `[Assumes: X]` declaration, or hop validity and arithmetic — none of which the chain-form table carries a column for — quote the analysis text directly. Folds in:
381	dead-end honesty, the no-analogies-as-direct-evidence ban (D-07), escape-valve policing for Abandoned
382	Reasoning (D-03), and hop validity and arithmetic. The one-line form is the degenerate case, used only when the whole chain fits on one physical line; a chain that does not fit uses the head-plus-arrow-led form, and a hop is split rather than continued on a second line.
383	
384	- **Rigorous** — every conclusion stated anywhere in the document (in section 4 or section 6)
385	  has exactly one derivation chain in section 4; each chain names the inputs it consumes — ground truths, upstream conclusions, or both — in the prescribed head form (`GT-1? ([brief fact label]) + C2 ([brief fact label])`),
386	  contains at least one intermediate claim (a claim that cannot be stated from any single named input alone), and reaches a conclusion; each chain is rendered in the prescribed
387	  arrow-led form. A hop occupies exactly one physical line. Every line after the head begins with `→` and carries exactly one complete hop; a hop is never broken across physical lines. The head line lists the inputs the chain consumes: each is a `GT-N` identifier (`GT-N?` when the ground truth is unverified) or a `Cn` identifier, optionally followed by a parenthesized gloss, joined to the next by `+`. The first `→` closes the head. An input carrying unparenthesized prose — `C2's threshold` — is not an identifier and does not parse; write `C2 (threshold)` in every position. The mechanical form check detects that violation only when the prose input is the last one before the first `→`; in an earlier position the check matches the well-formed remainder and scores the head conforming, so the rule binds in positions the check does not reach. The head grammar governs the head line only. A hop is prose: `C2's saving` is fine after the first `→`, and is not an input reference. One exception: a hop must not begin with a `GT-N` identifier, which the form check reads as the head of a new chain and which therefore ends this one — write `→ the duty cycle stated in GT-4 is the binding term`, not `→ GT-4's stated duty cycle is the binding term`. The form check detects that violation only while fewer than two hops precede it; in a later position the check matches the preceding hops and scores the chain conforming, so the rule binds in positions the check does not reach. The mechanical form check additionally rejects a chain whose head or first hop closes its own sentence before the next `→`: it reads the following arrow-led line as a new statement and ends the chain there, so a chain satisfying every rule above is scored malformed for that reason alone. The check reaches only that position — a hop that closes its own sentence from the second hop onward does not change the verdict — which is why intermediate hops carry no terminal punctuation in this project's worked examples. Hops rendered as an ordered list do not satisfy the prescribed form; the Abandoned Reasoning
388	  section either documents
389	  at least one dead end using the What-was-tried / Why-abandoned / What-it-ruled-out structure,
390	  OR uses the honest-depth escape valve with a reason that is specific to this analysis's
391	  problem and appears in no other analysis without alteration; no analogy
392	  is used as direct evidence (any reference to how others solved a similar problem is grounded
393	  in a named GT about their situation, not offered as standalone justification);
394	  each chain step that introduces an assumption not already in the Assumptions Table
395	  declares that assumption inline using `[Assumes: X]` appended to the step text —
396	  a reviewer applies this check by scanning each chain step for the `[Assumes:` token;
397	  and every hop the endpoint depends on follows from the line above it by deduction, by
398	  arithmetic that recomputes when redone independently of the chain text, or by a regularity
399	  cited to an unsuffixed ground truth — the test `output-template.md` states for the HIGH
400	  band under "Confidence levels, defined", shared here rather than restated. A hop that
401	  follows once the `[Assumes: X]` premise declared on that hop is granted counts as following
402	  for this criterion — declaring the premise takes the hop out of this limb by design, and
403	  whether that premise is priced is Criterion 5's Inference axis. An undeclared premise is not
404	  treated that way: a hop the endpoint depends on whose only gap is an undeclared premise is a
405	  non-sequitur under Hand-wavy below, and the `[Assumes: X]` limb above covers undeclared
406	  premises on hops the endpoint does not depend on; a hop citing
407	  a regularity to a `GT-N?` ground truth is an Inputs-axis matter Criterion 3/5 scores, not a
408	  failure to follow.
409	
410	- **Sound** — chains exist for all conclusions, but one or more chains lack a genuine
411	  intermediate step (the chain goes directly from its head inputs to conclusion, or the stated
412	  intermediate is a restatement of one of its named inputs rather than a new inference); OR
413	  a conclusion has more than one derivation chain — redundant restatement rather than a
414	  missing chain — where the prescribed form is exactly one chain per conclusion; OR
415	  one dead end in Abandoned Reasoning is described with a vague abandonment reason
416	  ("seemed unlikely," "ran out of time") rather than the specific structural reason
417	  (assumption false, contradicts a GT, circular, intermediate could not be established); OR
418	  one or more chains render their hops as an ordered list (`1.`, `2.`, `3.`) instead of the
419	  prescribed arrow-led hop form, OR break a single hop across physical lines rather than
420	  splitting it into two hops, which splits one chain into disconnected
421	  fragments even where every hop is individually sound; OR a hop fails to follow, or its
422	  arithmetic does not recompute, where the endpoint does not depend on that hop; OR a hop the
423	  endpoint depends on carries an arithmetic error that leaves the endpoint unchanged — the
424	  only case of a hop the endpoint depends on that this band admits, and it covers arithmetic
425	  only: a hop the endpoint depends on that does not follow by deduction or cited regularity is
426	  Hand-wavy, whatever the grader judges its effect on the endpoint — **this clause is why the criterion
427	  cannot be scored on reasoning quality alone.** A chain that names its inputs, carries a
428	  genuine intermediate and reaches a conclusion satisfies every other Rigorous requirement
429	  while still failing the prescribed form; scoring only the semantics is what lets a
430	  Rigorous verdict coexist with a section of malformed chains.

**Core problem:** Which single failure mechanism — and at which site of crack initiation (surface vs. subsurface) — actually drove this HSS-stage, generator-end cylindrical roller bearing to a spall at ~11% of its calculated L10 life, and does that mechanism match, partially match, or contradict the operator's stated cold-snap/low-viscosity/boundary-lubrication/wear-through hypothesis, to a level of evidentiary rigor sufficient to authorize a replacement-bearing specification and installation plan?

1. Each of the six named signatures (axial-aligned spalling, ~0.4 mm subsurface crescent microcracks, white-etching cracks, butterfly microstructure, kurtosis-based detection, L10 ratio) is explicitly mapped, via a cited ground truth, to a diagnosed mechanism, mode, and site of initiation — a skeptic can find, for every signature named in the brief, the sentence that says what it means and why.

6. The answer is not forced into exactly one of the operator's two implied buckets ("it's the lubricant" / "it's not the lubricant"); a combined or partially-overlapping finding is explicitly tested for and reported if the evidence supports it.

## 3. Ground Truths

Two evidentiary classes appear below. **Case-stipulated direct observations** (GT-1 through
GT-6) are this investigation's own disassembly, condition-monitoring, and metallurgical findings
as given in the failure brief — they are direct measurements/observations, the irreducibility

read-at-source test is satisfied by "this is what the investigating team directly measured,"
with the brief itself as the record. **External literature ground truths** (GT-7 onward) are
claims about what such signatures generally mean in the wind-turbine-bearing failure-analysis
literature, each carrying the provenance label this session's own research activity earned it —
`read-at-source` only where this analysis itself fetched the specific page and the quote below
was checked against it, `reported-by-delegate` where a search tool's aggregated summary supplied
the claim without this analysis opening the underlying document.

**Case-stipulated direct observations:**

- **GT-1** 1.5 MW upwind turbine; HSS gearbox stage; generator-end position; bearing type cylindrical roller — source: failure brief (disassembly/unit identification); read-at-source: Failure Context, as given.
- **GT-2** Condition monitoring flagged a step increase in HSS vibration kurtosis at ~14,000 operating hours; bearing pulled at that point — source: failure brief (condition-monitoring record); read-at-source: Failure Context, as given.
- **GT-3** L10 design life for this bearing/application ≈130,000 h (per design calculation) ⇒ failure/L10 ratio ≈11% — source: failure brief (design-life figure); read-at-source: Failure Context, as given.
- **GT-4** Inner race shows axial-aligned spalling, ≈18 mm long — source: failure brief (disassembly/visual inspection); read-at-source: Physical/Metallurgical Evidence, as given.
- **GT-5** Crescent-shaped microcracks propagate from a subsurface origin ≈0.4 mm below the raceway surface — source: failure brief (metallographic sectioning); read-at-source: Physical/Metallurgical Evidence, as given.
- **GT-6** Metallographic sections through the spall show white-etching cracks (WEC) and butterfly microstructure at inclusions/subsurface stress risers — source: failure brief (metallography); read-at-source: Physical/Metallurgical Evidence, as given.

**External literature ground truths:**

- **GT-7** WEC/axial-cracking failures in wind-turbine gearbox bearings "commonly...have occurred within the first one to three years of operational time or at 5 to 10% of the calculated rating life" — source: SKF, "Premature bearing failures in wind gearboxes and white etching cracks (WEC)," evolution.skf.com; read-at-source: article body, quoted sentence fetched and checked directly this session.
- **GT-8** Axial cracks propagate "radially and axially" (not circumferentially); subsurface origin "at depths up to the depth to maximum Hertzian shear stress"; occur mainly on HSS/intermediate-shaft cylindrical and spherical roller bearing inner races; WEA/butterfly microstructural mechanism described as distinct from surface wear/micropitting, which the source treats as "a separate document," i.e. a different mechanism — source: Scott Hyde (Timken), Gear Solutions magazine, "Axial Cracking" article, 6 May 2014, gearsolutions.com; read-at-source: article body, fetched and quoted directly this session.
- **GT-9** L10 life is formally "the theoretical life that 90 percent of a bearing population should equal or exceed... at their operating load"; "10 percent of the bearings... can be expected to fail" before L10 is reached — a single early failure is, in isolation, statistically anticipated in a population and not by itself anomalous — source: machinerylubrication.com, "How to Determine Bearing System Life"; read-at-source: article body, fetched and quoted directly this session.

boundary-lubrication wear could have receded the raceway surface enough that a defect which
actually originated at the (original) surface now measures as "0.4 mm below the surface" relative
to the new, worn-down surface — i.e., rescuing the operator's hypothesis by reinterpreting the
depth measurement rather than contesting it.

**Why abandoned:** Two problems. First, 0.4 mm (400 µm) of uniform material loss from boundary
lubrication wear on a hardened raceway is itself a visually obvious, large-scale wear event that

measurement is framed. The hypothesis fails on the same ground truth that defeats Dead End 1.

arguing about the depth measurement's reference frame rather than its mechanism; chain C2 cites
this dead end as part of its own internal reasoning (it is the "artifact" alternative hop 4 rules
out).

### Dead End 3: A single lightning-strike transient, rather than chronic converter-driven shaft voltage, is the electrical driver

**What was tried:** Because this is an upwind turbine with direct lightning exposure through the
blades and drivetrain, considered whether a single large lightning-induced current transient
(rather than chronic low-level PWM-converter shaft voltage) was the electrical mechanism bearing

failure's own timeline. GT-2's detection signal is a *step increase* in an impulsive vibration

discharge-site evidence (or absence of it) that test is designed to find.

## Adversarial pass (process output)

**Recompute.** The only computed figure in this analysis is GT-3's failure/L10 ratio:
14,000 h ÷ 130,000 h = 0.1077 → 10.8%, which rounds to the stated "~11%." Recomputed
independently of the chain text and confirmed; no arithmetic error. No other chain performs
arithmetic.

**Sensitivity.** The single ground truth whose falsity would flip the headline conclusion is
**GT-6** (white-etching cracks + butterfly microstructure at the metallographic section) — it is
not `?`-marked (it is a direct case observation), but it is the one fact every WEC-identifying
chain (C2, C4, C5, C9) ultimately depends on, and this analysis did not independently re-examine
the metallography itself. If GT-6 were an etching artifact or a non-representative section
(assumption A-10), the entire WEC/hydrogen case collapses toward either classical subsurface RCF
or, if GT-2/GT-5's depth reading were also reinterpreted, back toward the operator's original
hypothesis. This is the same finding Cluster A below acts on. Per-chain weakest links: C4 and C8
are the two weakest chains in this analysis, both resting on literature this session did not open
at the primary source (GT-12?/GT-13?/GT-18? for C4; GT-14?/GT-15? for C8) rather than on this
bearing's own test data.

**Rival.** Headline conclusion (C9, "verified WEC-class mechanism"): rival = ordinary classical
inclusion-driven subsurface RCF, ruled out by C5 and Dead End 1 (statistics) / the metallurgy
itself (GT-6). Intermediate chain C6 ("operator's hypothesis rejected as direct mechanism"):
rival = "the operator is still partly right" — not ruled out, carried forward live as C7 (a
revised, lower-confidence role for lubricant condition). Intermediate chain C8 ("electrical
stray current live"): rival = "hydrogen/lubricant pathway alone, no electrical contribution" —
this rival is **not** ruled out and stays live; it is exactly why C8 and everything built on it
(C10, C11, the Conclusion) are capped at MEDIUM rather than HIGH.

**Premise.** The headline conclusion is already false: this bearing's failure was *not*
caused by subsurface hydrogen-assisted white-etching-crack cracking. What caused that error?

**Causes** (unfiltered, by stakeholder viewpoint, generated before any grouping):
- *Skeptical independent metallurgist:* the metallographic section was non-representative
  (A-10) and the "white-etching" call is an over-etching artifact; the "butterflies" are
  ordinary classical-fatigue butterflies (butterflies are not WEC-exclusive) and labeling them
  WEC overstates the case; no hydrogen-content/SIMS measurement was actually performed on this
  bearing's own steel, so the WEC call rests on optical metallography alone.
- *Bearing OEM warranty/engineering reviewer:* the L10 calculation may have used outdated or
  generic load inputs (A-5), making "~11%" an artifact of the calculation rather than of the
  bearing's real behavior; the bearing may have been mishandled or misaligned at installation,
  producing accelerated but ordinary subsurface stress that only coincidentally matches WEC-
  population statistics; no material certificate (A-11) confirms this bearing's steel batch met
  spec, so this could be an ordinary quality escape, not an industry WEC phenomenon.
- *Operator's reliability engineer:* the cold-snap/viscosity hypothesis (A-1) was never actually
  tested against real temperature/viscosity logs, so it may still be correct and this analysis's
  rejection of it premature; the kurtosis alarm threshold (A-4) may itself be miscalibrated, so
  the "step increase at 14,000 h" could be exaggerated or spurious; no sister unit on the same
  platform/lubricant regime has been checked, so there is no confirmation this is systemic rather
  than a one-off.
- *Turbine/gearbox OEM design engineer:* the grounding brush and bearing insulation (A-7, A-8)
  were never field-inspected before this conclusion was drafted, so the electrical pathway this
  analysis itself calls "unresolved" could in fact be dominant; this turbine's lightning-
  protection-system condition was never checked, and Dead End 3 may have set aside a genuine
  lightning-transient pathway too quickly.

**Clusters** (structural weaknesses the causes above fall into, with the chain/GT ids each
bears on):
- **Cluster A — metallurgical-call reliability** (bears on GT-6, A-10, chains C2/C4/C9): the
  entire WEC identification rests on one optical metallographic reading this analysis did not
  re-examine.
- **Cluster B — L10/statistics artifact** (bears on GT-3, A-5, chain C3): the "~11%" figure's
  evidentiary weight depends on the original L10 calculation being sound and on normal
  installation practice.
- **Cluster C — steel-quality/material escape** (bears on A-11, chain C5): classical RCF was
  downgraded partly on a cleanliness assumption this analysis could not verify.
- **Cluster D — operator-hypothesis/CM-data reliability** (bears on A-1, A-4, A-6, chains
  C1/C6/C7): the rejection of the operator's hypothesis, and the detection timeline it rests on,
  both depend on CM and lubricant data this analysis never saw directly.
- **Cluster E — electrical/lightning pathway understated** (bears on GT-15?, A-7, A-8, chain
  C8/C10, Dead End 3): the one genuinely unresolved rival in this entire analysis is also the
  one this analysis had the least direct evidence about.

**Disposition** (per cluster):
- **Cluster A — plan change:** before this analysis's conclusion is used in any warranty or
  liability determination, commission an independent re-section and a hydrogen-content/SIMS
  analysis of the retained steel (this is the same verification C4's confidence line already
  names); do not let the final determination rest on optical metallography alone.
- **Cluster B — plan change:** re-audit the original L10 calculation's load-spectrum and duty-
  cycle inputs (A-5) and review the installation/mounting records before citing the ~11% ratio
  as confirmed evidence of an anomalous mechanism in any formal report.
- **Cluster C — accepted risk, named mitigation:** request the mill certificate/inclusion
  rating (A-11) retroactively from the bearing supplier; if it cannot be obtained, accept the
  residual uncertainty explicitly in the warranty determination rather than treating classical
  RCF as fully excluded.
- **Cluster D — plan change:** pull the actual SCADA temperature/viscosity log for the cold-snap
  period and the CM system's self-diagnostic/calibration record (A-1, A-4) before finalizing;
  inspect at least one sister unit's generator-end bearing on the same platform and lubricant
  regime.
- **Cluster E — plan change:** elevate the shaft-current/insulation-resistance test and a
  lightning-protection-system condition check from "recommended" to "mandatory before sign-off"
  — this cluster is the one place in the whole analysis where a rival fully capable of becoming
  the primary cause remains genuinely live and untested.

**Falsification.** The conclusion is false if an independent re-section and hydrogen-content/
SIMS analysis of this bearing's retained steel finds no hydrogen enrichment and no genuine
white-etching alteration at the crack network (overturning GT-6 as a sectioning/etching
artifact), **or** if direct re-inspection finds macroscopic surface material loss/scoring
consistent with ~0.4 mm of wear-driven surface recession (reopening Dead End 2 with physical
evidence this analysis did not have).

Investigate and verify the root cause of a premature wind turbine gearbox bearing failure. This is a real engineering failure analysis to authorize a replacement bearing specification — the conclusion needs to be defensible, not just plausible.

FAILURE CONTEXT:
- 1.5 MW upwind wind turbine, high-speed-shaft (HSS) gearbox stage, generator-end bearing.
- Bearing type: cylindrical roller bearing.
- Removed from service after condition monitoring flagged a step increase in HSS vibration kurtosis at ~14,000 operating hours.
- L10 design life for this bearing/application was ~130,000 hours — so failure occurred at roughly 11% of design life, an order of magnitude early.

PHYSICAL/METALLURGICAL EVIDENCE ON DISASSEMBLY:
- Inner race: axial-aligned spalling, roughly 18 mm long.
- Crescent-shaped microcracks propagating from a subsurface origin approximately 0.4 mm below the raceway surface.
- Metallographic sections through the spall show white-etching cracks (WEC) and a butterfly microstructure (classic butterfly wings at inclusions/subsurface stress risers).

OPERATOR'S STATED HYPOTHESIS (to be stress-tested, not assumed correct):
"Lubricant failed — viscosity was too low during a cold-snap period, which drove the bearing into boundary lubrication, and the race wore through."

YOUR TASK:
1. Decompose the failure into verified ground truths: what do the specific physical signatures (axial-aligned spalling, subsurface crescent microcracks at ~0.4mm depth, white-etching cracks, butterfly microstructure, kurtosis-based detection, L10 life ratio) actually indicate about failure mechanism, mode, and site of initiation (surface-initiated wear vs. subsurface-initiated rolling contact fatigue)?
2. Explicitly test the operator's cold-snap/low-viscosity/boundary-lubrication/wear-through hypothesis against the physical evidence. Boundary lubrication and abrasive/adhesive wear produce characteristic surface morphology (surface-initiated distress, scuffing, material loss at the surface) — determine whether that is consistent or inconsistent with subsurface-originated WEC + butterflies + crescent cracks at depth.
3. Consider and weigh alternative/competing root causes known to produce WEC and butterflies in wind turbine HSS gearbox bearings specifically — e.g., hydrogen-assisted subsurface cracking (from lubricant degradation, moisture/water contamination, or tribochemical reactions), electrical stray-current damage (common at generator-end bearings due to shaft currents from the generator/converter), classical subsurface-initiated rolling contact fatigue from inclusions/overload, or other mechanisms — and determine which mechanism is actually consistent with ALL the evidence (location at generator end, axial orientation of spalling, 0.4mm subsurface origin depth, WEC+butterflies, kurtosis onset at 14k hrs vs 130k hr L10).
4. Reach and justify a single verified root cause (or ranked set if evidence is genuinely ambiguous), explicitly stating why the operator's lubricant-viscosity hypothesis is correct, partially correct, or should be rejected — and what evidence would further discriminate between remaining candidates if needed (e.g., shaft current / grounding measurements, oil analysis for moisture/additive depletion, hydrogen content analysis of the steel, insulation resistance checks on the generator bearing).
5. State what this means for the replacement bearing specification and installation (e.g., insulated bearing or grounding brush if stray current is implicated, vs. lubricant/breather/heater changes if lubrication is implicated, vs. inspection of upstream causes if inclusion-driven RCF).

Report back with the full reasoned analysis: the decomposition, the hypothesis test, the competing causes considered and why rejected, and the final verified root cause with its confidence level and the specific evidence that drives that confidence.

1	# Wind Turbine Gearbox Bearing Premature Failure Root Cause
2	
3	*First-principles analysis · 9 October 2026*
4	
5	*Read with: [How to read this analysis](HOW-TO-READ.md) · [Working file](analysis-20261009T203449Z.md) · [All files](INDEX.md)*
6	
7	## Executive Summary
8	
9	**Recommendation:** Authorize the replacement bearing specification as a combined mechanical-metallurgical, lubrication-chemistry, and electrical-verification package — not the operator's viscosity-only fix — because the verified root cause is subsurface, hydrogen-assisted, white-etching-crack-class rolling-contact fatigue, not boundary-lubrication wear-through (chain C11).
10	
11	**Band (from §6):** MEDIUM — capped by C6, C9, C10 and C11, each MEDIUM (chain C9).
12	
13	**Would change it:** Opening the primary WEC/hydrogen literature (GT-12?, GT-13?, GT-18?) at source, and running the shaft-current/insulation-resistance test that chain C8 proposes to resolve the live electrical rival carried in chain C10, would move the band toward HIGH.
14	
15	## 1. Problem Essence
16	
17	**Core problem:** Which single failure mechanism — and at which site of crack initiation (surface vs. subsurface) — actually drove this HSS-stage, generator-end cylindrical roller bearing to a spall at ~11% of its calculated L10 life, and does that mechanism match, partially match, or contradict the operator's stated cold-snap/low-viscosity/boundary-lubrication/wear-through hypothesis, to a level of evidentiary rigor sufficient to authorize a replacement-bearing specification and installation plan?
18	
19	**Success criteria:**
20	1. Each of the six named signatures (axial-aligned spalling, ~0.4 mm subsurface crescent microcracks, white-etching cracks, butterfly microstructure, kurtosis-based detection, L10 ratio) is explicitly mapped, via a cited ground truth, to a diagnosed mechanism, mode, and site of initiation — a skeptic can find, for every signature named in the brief, the sentence that says what it means and why.
21	2. The operator's hypothesis is tested — not assumed true or false — against the subsurface-origin evidence, and the analysis states an explicit accept/partial/reject verdict naming the specific morphological discriminator that drives it.
22	3. Hydrogen-assisted WEC, classical inclusion-driven subsurface RCF, and generator-end electrical stray current are each weighed against *all* of the physical evidence given (not a convenient subset), with an explicit consistent/inconsistent/unresolved verdict for each.
23	4. A verified root cause — or an explicitly ranked/multi-factorial set, if the evidence genuinely does not collapse to one cause — is stated with a confidence band and the specific test(s) (oil analysis, shaft-current/insulation-resistance measurement, steel cleanliness certificate, L10-input re-audit) that would move that band.
24	5. The replacement-bearing specification and installation plan is derived from, and traceable to, the determined root cause — not generic bearing-replacement boilerplate.
25	6. The answer is not forced into exactly one of the operator's two implied buckets ("it's the lubricant" / "it's not the lubricant"); a combined or partially-overlapping finding is explicitly tested for and reported if the evidence supports it.
26	
27	## 2. Assumptions Table
28	
29	![Assumption verdict matrix: assumption types against verdicts](report-20261009T203449Z-fig-verdicts.svg)
30	
31	**Cause-space brainstorm (fishbone, 6M set — applied because the candidate-mechanism space is
32	genuinely multi-causal and intuition alone cannot enumerate it with confidence).** Categories
33	walked: Machine (bearing design/steel cleanliness/heat treatment), Method (mounting, preload,
34	fit), Material (lubricant chemistry, moisture, steel inclusions), Measurement (CM calibration,
35	detection lag), Man (maintenance lapses on grounding brushes, wrong lubricant top-up), Mother
36	Nature/Environment (cold-snap, moisture ingress, grid transients, lightning — this is an upwind
37	turbine, directly lightning-exposed). Each branch below either resolves into one of the
38	assumptions in the table or is carried forward as a competing-cause chain in section 4. No
39	category produced a candidate that required a new assumption *beyond* those discriminable below;
40	the branch that most needed a discriminating observation — "is this electrical or chemical?" —
41	is exactly the one section 4 (chains C8/C10) and the Conclusion name as unresolved pending field
42	test, which is the fishbone procedure's own honest-no-discriminator outcome, not a gap in this scan.
43	
44	**Inversion (applied because an early draft conclusion — "it's WEC" — risked being too clean a
45	pattern-match to a fashionable modern diagnosis).** Inverted claim: "the verified root cause is
46	NOT subsurface hydrogen-assisted WEC." Failure-guaranteeing conditions enumerated: (i) the
47	reported subsurface origin depth is an artifact of surface material already lost to wear,
48	making a post-wear surface look "subsurface" relative to the new, receded surface; (ii) the
49	white-etching/butterfly microstructure is a sectioning or etching artifact, not a real
50	in-service feature; (iii) the axial orientation is coincidental, not diagnostic, because axial
51	cracking also occurs in non-WEC overload failures; (iv) the L10 ratio is unremarkable ordinary
52	statistical scatter, and WEC is being read into an otherwise ordinary early fatigue failure;
53	(v) electrical stray current — not hydrogen/lubricant chemistry — is the actual driver, and the
54	"WEC" label is mechanism-agnostic physical evidence that both pathways produce identically.
55	Necessary preconditions derived from these, tagged load-bearing or not, and their verification
56	status are carried into the table below as A-9, A-10, and the competing-cause chains C5/C8; (i)
57	and (ii) are addressed directly in section 4 (C2, Abandoned Reasoning) rather than restated here.
58	
59	| Assumption | Type | Treatment | Verdict | Verification |
60	|------------|------|-----------|---------|--------------|
61	| A-1: The lubricant viscosity was in fact below the OEM-specified minimum during the cited cold-snap period | untested belief | Verify or flag | Challenge — no viscosity-vs-temperature log or oil sample was supplied to confirm the operator's premise | unverified — flagged |
62	| A-2: Boundary lubrication / low-film-thickness operation characteristically produces surface-initiated wear distress, not subsurface-originated cracking | convention, challenged and elevated | Challenge before use, then accept on verification | Accept — confirmed by GT-11 (ISO-15243-aligned classification), read at source | read-at-source: GT-11 |
63	| A-3: Hertzian rolling contact produces a subsurface shear-stress maximum at a characteristic depth, and classical subsurface fatigue nucleates there | physical law | Accept as ground-truth candidate | Accept — standard contact-mechanics theory, consistent with GT-5/GT-6/GT-12 | promoted to GT-17? (background theory, not independently re-opened this session) |
64	| A-4: The kurtosis step-increase at ~14,000 hours accurately reflects bearing distress and is not a CM sensor/calibration artifact | untested belief | Verify or flag | Challenge — no CM self-diagnostic/calibration record was supplied | unverified — flagged |
65	| A-5: The stated L10 design life (~130,000 h) was correctly calculated for this unit's actual historical load spectrum, speed, and duty cycle | untested belief (high-stakes) | Verify or flag | Challenge — if the design-life input was understated, part of the apparent "prematurity" could be a calculation artifact rather than purely an anomalous mechanism | unverified — flagged |
66	| A-6: No independent operational anomaly (grid fault, overload, contamination ingress, prior over-torque assembly) occurred that alone explains the early failure | untested belief | Verify or flag | Challenge — absence of evidence is not evidence of absence | unverified — flagged |
67	| A-7: This turbine's generator/converter topology is converter-fed (e.g., DFIG or full-converter) and subject to PWM-driven common-mode/shaft-voltage behavior | current constraint | Record expiry conditions | Challenge — drivetrain electrical topology is not stated in the case | unverified — flagged; expires once nameplate/drawing confirms topology |
68	| A-8: A shaft-grounding brush system is fitted to this unit's generator and was functioning as designed up to the failure | untested belief | Verify or flag | Challenge — not stated in the case | unverified — flagged |
69	| A-9: "Axial-aligned spalling" means the spall's long axis runs parallel to the bearing's rotational axis, per standard wind-bearing-failure usage | convention | Challenge before use | Accept — standard usage, cross-checked against GT-8's terminology | read-at-source: GT-8 |
70	| A-10: The metallographic section showing WEC/butterflies was taken through a representative region of the spall origin, per standard failure-analysis practice | convention / standard practice | Challenge/accept per standard practice | Accept — standard destructive failure-analysis practice assumed; no raw micrographs were supplied to this analysis | unverified — flagged |
71	| A-11: This bearing's steel cleanliness and heat treatment meet modern premium bearing-steel manufacturing standards | untested belief | Verify or flag | Challenge — no mill certificate / inclusion-rating (e.g., ASTM E45/DIN 50602) was supplied | unverified — flagged |
72	| A-12: This HSS bearing experiences meaningful slip/skidding under the turbine's actual partial-load, variable-wind, idling profile | untested belief | Verify or flag | Challenge — plausible for a variable-speed HSS stage but not confirmed for this unit | unverified — flagged |
73	| A-13: A WEC-resistant or electrically-insulated replacement bearing in the required envelope is available within an acceptable lead time | current constraint | Record expiry conditions | Challenge — not confirmed | unverified — flagged; expires once OEM/supplier confirms a qualified part number |
74	| A-14: Hydrogen-assisted cracking is a physically valid degradation mechanism in high-strength bearing steel under combined stress and atomic hydrogen exposure | physical law | Accept as ground-truth candidate | Accept — well-established materials science, corroborated by GT-13? | promoted to GT-18? (corroborated, not independently re-opened this session) |
75	
76	## 3. Ground Truths
77	
78	Two evidentiary classes appear below. **Case-stipulated direct observations** (GT-1 through
79	GT-6) are this investigation's own disassembly, condition-monitoring, and metallurgical findings
80	as given in the failure brief — they are direct measurements/observations, the irreducibility
81	test's third admissible category, and are not citations to external literature, so the
82	read-at-source test is satisfied by "this is what the investigating team directly measured,"
83	with the brief itself as the record. **External literature ground truths** (GT-7 onward) are
84	claims about what such signatures generally mean in the wind-turbine-bearing failure-analysis
85	literature, each carrying the provenance label this session's own research activity earned it —
86	`read-at-source` only where this analysis itself fetched the specific page and the quote below
87	was checked against it, `reported-by-delegate` where a search tool's aggregated summary supplied
88	the claim without this analysis opening the underlying document.
89	
90	**Case-stipulated direct observations:**
91	
92	- **GT-1** 1.5 MW upwind turbine; HSS gearbox stage; generator-end position; bearing type cylindrical roller — source: failure brief (disassembly/unit identification); read-at-source: Failure Context, as given.
93	- **GT-2** Condition monitoring flagged a step increase in HSS vibration kurtosis at ~14,000 operating hours; bearing pulled at that point — source: failure brief (condition-monitoring record); read-at-source: Failure Context, as given.
94	- **GT-3** L10 design life for this bearing/application ≈130,000 h (per design calculation) ⇒ failure/L10 ratio ≈11% — source: failure brief (design-life figure); read-at-source: Failure Context, as given.
95	- **GT-4** Inner race shows axial-aligned spalling, ≈18 mm long — source: failure brief (disassembly/visual inspection); read-at-source: Physical/Metallurgical Evidence, as given.
96	- **GT-5** Crescent-shaped microcracks propagate from a subsurface origin ≈0.4 mm below the raceway surface — source: failure brief (metallographic sectioning); read-at-source: Physical/Metallurgical Evidence, as given.
97	- **GT-6** Metallographic sections through the spall show white-etching cracks (WEC) and butterfly microstructure at inclusions/subsurface stress risers — source: failure brief (metallography); read-at-source: Physical/Metallurgical Evidence, as given.
98	
99	**External literature ground truths:**
100	
101	- **GT-7** WEC/axial-cracking failures in wind-turbine gearbox bearings "commonly...have occurred within the first one to three years of operational time or at 5 to 10% of the calculated rating life" — source: SKF, "Premature bearing failures in wind gearboxes and white etching cracks (WEC)," evolution.skf.com; read-at-source: article body, quoted sentence fetched and checked directly this session.
102	- **GT-8** Axial cracks propagate "radially and axially" (not circumferentially); subsurface origin "at depths up to the depth to maximum Hertzian shear stress"; occur mainly on HSS/intermediate-shaft cylindrical and spherical roller bearing inner races; WEA/butterfly microstructural mechanism described as distinct from surface wear/micropitting, which the source treats as "a separate document," i.e. a different mechanism — source: Scott Hyde (Timken), Gear Solutions magazine, "Axial Cracking" article, 6 May 2014, gearsolutions.com; read-at-source: article body, fetched and quoted directly this session.
103	- **GT-9** L10 life is formally "the theoretical life that 90 percent of a bearing population should equal or exceed... at their operating load"; "10 percent of the bearings... can be expected to fail" before L10 is reached — a single early failure is, in isolation, statistically anticipated in a population and not by itself anomalous — source: machinerylubrication.com, "How to Determine Bearing System Life"; read-at-source: article body, fetched and quoted directly this session.
104	- **GT-10** Electrical/stray-current discharge characteristically produces surface-level signatures — "frosting," "spark tracks (sometimes called worm tracks)," "burned spots and spot welding," and at higher energy "electrodischarge machining (EDM)... with very significant material removal" — occurring "at points of contact or near contact," i.e. surface-initiated, not reported as producing a subsurface crescent-crack network — source: power-eng.com, "Stray currents can damage turbine bearings"; read-at-source: article body, fetched and quoted directly this session.
105	- **GT-11** Surface-initiated fatigue "begins at the contact surface, triggered by... inadequate lubrication, contamination dents, handling or installation damage," producing "arrowhead-shaped spalls," "irregular shape, jagged edges, shallow craters" concentrated at edges; subsurface-initiated fatigue "begins below the raceway surface, at inclusions or material discontinuities," is "the bearing's expected fatigue life," producing "elliptically shaped spalls at the center of the raceway" — a different site and a different morphology from surface wear — source: reliabilitysolutions.net, "Bearing Spalling: How It Starts, How It Spreads"; read-at-source: article body, fetched and quoted directly this session; corroborated (not separately IDed) by an SKF/ISO 15243 damage-classification aggregate obtained via search this session.
106	- **GT-12?** WEC crack networks in wind-turbine gearbox bearings have been documented attached to MnS inclusions at subsurface depths up to ~630 µm, extending to the depth of maximum subsurface shear stress — cited to: University of Southampton WEC serial-sectioning research (Evans et al.); reported-by-delegate: WebSearch aggregate summary — cited source not opened directly by this analysis.
107	- **GT-13?** Hydrogen-assisted cracking is implicated as a contributing/accelerating mechanism for WEC, with hydrogen entering via lubricant decomposition and/or tribochemical reaction with water at the contact surface or at surface-breaching cracks; named contributing factors include lubricant chemistry/moisture, slip/skidding, and electrical current, acting in combination rather than any single one alone — cited to: Southampton/Springer tribology literature aggregate (incl. 108	- **GT-14?** Low-level electrical discharge (literature cites currents below ~200 µA) has been proposed as a WEC-forming/catalyzing driver via localized thermal/microstructural effects, independent of the macroscopic EDM pitting/fluting associated with gross stray-current damage — cited to: STLE/MPIE electromagnetic-WEC-hypothesis literature aggregate; reported-by-delegate: WebSearch aggregate summary — cited source not opened directly by this analysis.

110	- **GT-16?** Kurtosis is a vibration-signal statistic specifically sensitive to impulsive, non-Gaussian content, which is why it is used as an early condition-monitoring indicator of a discrete, nucleating rolling-element defect ahead of broadband RMS trending — standard vibration-analysis engineering knowledge; unverified: no source was opened for this specific claim during this session.
111	- **GT-17?** Hertzian rolling contact produces a subsurface orthogonal shear-stress maximum at a characteristic depth below the contact surface, scaling with contact half-width — standard contact-mechanics theory (Hertz/Lundberg-Palmgren); unverified: not independently re-opened at a primary source this session, promoted from assumption A-3.
112	- **GT-18?** Hydrogen-assisted cracking is a recognized materials-degradation mechanism in high-strength steels under combined mechanical stress and atomic hydrogen exposure — standard materials-science background theory, corroborated by GT-13?; unverified: not independently re-opened at a primary source this session, promoted from assumption A-14.
113	
114	**Provenance summary (required):**
115

133	GT-2 (kurtosis step-increase, ~14,000 h) + GT-16? (kurtosis sensitive to impulsive content)
134	→ kurtosis specifically flags impulsive, non-Gaussian vibration content rather than gradual broadband amplitude growth [Assumes: A-4]

171	### Conclusion C5: Ordinary classical inclusion-driven subsurface fatigue is not the primary mechanism here
172	
173	GT-6 (WEC + butterfly, specifically white-etching) + GT-11 (modern clean steels make ordinary subsurface fatigue rare) + C3 (HIGH)
174	→ modern bearing-steel cleanliness and processing make ordinary unaltered subsurface-initiated fatigue comparatively rare, per GT-11's classification [Assumes: A-11]

179	**Confidence:** HIGH — hop 1's [Assumes: A-11] (steel cleanliness) is priced: if A-11 fails, classical RCF becomes more plausible as a background contributor, but the conclusion that classical RCF is not primary is unaffected, because hops 2 and 3 independently establish the WEC-population match through microstructure and through C3's statistical/orientation match, neither of which depends on A-11.

181	### Conclusion C6: The operator's boundary-lubrication/wear-through hypothesis is rejected as the direct mechanism
182	
183	C2 (MEDIUM) + C4 (MEDIUM)
184	→ the operator's proposed mechanism requires the damage to originate at the contact surface via metal-to-metal asperity contact, which is the opposite of what C2 establishes for this bearing

191	
192	C4 (MEDIUM) + GT-13? (lubricant/moisture/slip hydrogen-generation pathway)
193	→ lubricant chemistry, moisture and additive breakdown, and slip/skidding are established, per GT-13, as contributing or catalyzing inputs to hydrogen-assisted WEC formation
194	→ a real lubricant-condition deficiency could therefore still be causally relevant to the mechanism established in C4, just through a different pathway than the direct wear-through one the operator named

197	→ the operator's "lubricant condition mattered" intuition is therefore plausibly partially correct, but only in this revised causal role as a hydrogen-generation catalyst, not as the direct wear-through mechanism C6 already rejected

199	**Confidence:** MEDIUM — capped by C4 (MEDIUM) and by GT-13? (reported-by-delegate); hop 3 also carries unpriced [Assumes: A-1][Assumes: A-12]; verification: oil analysis for moisture content, acid number and additive depletion, cross-checked against the dated cold-snap period (A-1), plus a skid/borescope check for slip evidence on lightly-loaded rollers (A-12).

201	### Conclusion C8: Generator-end electrical stray current is a live, unresolved competing or contributing cause

204	→ the generator-end location is, per GT-15, the specific site in a converter-fed drivetrain where capacitively-coupled shaft voltage and current are most commonly introduced, so electrical stray current cannot be dismissed on location grounds alone [Assumes: A-7][Assumes: A-8]

211	### Conclusion C9: The verified root cause is subsurface, hydrogen-assisted, white-etching-crack-class rolling-contact fatigue

214	→ together, C2 and C4 establish the verified failure class at this HSS generator-end inner race: subsurface-initiated, microstructurally-altered, hydrogen-assisted rolling-contact cracking, i.e. white-etching-crack-class damage

221	### Conclusion C10: The full causal picture is ranked and multi-factorial, not a single clean cause
222	
223	C7 (MEDIUM) + C8 (MEDIUM) + C9 (MEDIUM)
224	→ a genuine lubricant-condition deficiency, in the revised causal role C7 establishes as a hydrogen-generation catalyst rather than a direct wear-through agent, remains a plausible but unverified contributor to the mechanism C9 identifies

226	→ neither C7 nor C8 displaces the mechanism identification in C9; both instead describe candidate accelerants or co-contributors whose relative weight is not yet resolved
227	→ the primary, established cause is the verified WEC-class subsurface mechanism in C9
228	→ the best-supported secondary candidate is the lubricant-chemistry/slip contribution in C7
229	→ generator-end electrical stray current (C8) remains a live, unresolved competing or co-contributing candidate
230	→ the operator's literal wear-through mechanism and ordinary classical fatigue are both excluded as primary explanations
231	
232	**Confidence:** MEDIUM — capped by C7, C8 and C9, each MEDIUM; no additional downgrade cause belongs to this chain itself.
233	
234	### Conclusion C11: The replacement specification must be a combined mechanical-metallurgical, lubrication-chemistry and electrical-verification package
235	
236	C9 (MEDIUM) + C10 (MEDIUM)
237	→ because the primary verified mechanism established in C9 is subsurface hydrogen-assisted WEC rather than simple lubricant wear-through, the replacement bearing and its installation must directly address the WEC risk pathway
238	→ addressing that pathway means lubricant chemistry and moisture control plus WEC-resistant metallurgy or surface treatment, not increased oil viscosity alone
239	→ because electrical stray current is unresolved rather than excluded in C10, and the generator-end position is specifically where shaft-current damage enters a converter-fed drivetrain, the plan must also include a direct electrical verification track

241	→ the replacement-bearing specification and installation plan must therefore be a combined mechanical-metallurgical, lubrication-chemistry, and electrical-verification package
242	→ it must not rely on the operator's original viscosity-only remedy as sufficient on its own
243	→[2nd] if this specification is applied only to the failed unit, sister turbines sharing the same platform, generator/converter topology, and lubricant regime carry the same unverified risk

246	→[3rd] treating this as a single bearing-level fix rather than a platform-level finding, across several replacement cycles, risks normalizing a recurring WEC failure as routine "early wear," eroding the L10-based maintenance-planning assumption (A-5) fleet-wide
247

249	
250	**Unverified input rule (D-07) summary:** C1, C2, C4, C7, C8 each carry a `GT-N?` input directly and are capped at MEDIUM accordingly, with the removing verification named on each chain's own confidence line. C3 and C5 are the two chains in this analysis rated HIGH, and neither consumes a `GT-N?` input.
251	
252	## 5. Abandoned Reasoning
253	
254	### Dead End 1: Ordinary L10 statistical scatter explains the early failure, no special mechanism needed
255	
256	**What was tried:** Treated the ~11% L10 ratio as nothing more than the expected population-level
257	scatter GT-9 describes (some bearings in any population fail before L10 by definition), with no
258	need to invoke WEC or any other non-classical mechanism — i.e., this bearing is simply one of the
259	unlucky ~10%.
260	
261	**Why abandoned:** This reading is contradicted by GT-6 and GT-7 together. GT-6 is a direct
262	metallurgical finding of white-etching cracks and butterfly microstructure, which is not a
263	signature ordinary, unaltered inclusion-driven fatigue produces — "ordinary scatter" has no
264	mechanism that explains why the metallography would show a nanocrystalline, acid-etch-resistant
265	altered microstructure. GT-7 independently shows the specific ~11% ratio sits inside the narrow
266	5–10% band documented for the WEC-driven failure population, not spread uniformly across the 0–100%
267	range ordinary scatter would predict. The reading is not merely weak, it is actively contradicted
268	by a ground truth (GT-6), so it was discarded rather than merely downgraded.
269	
270	**What it ruled out:** Saves a reviewer from re-litigating "maybe this is just bad luck" — the
271	metallurgy alone (independent of any statistical argument) already answers that question; chain
272	C3 cites this dead end as its Rivals-axis discharge.
273	
274	### Dead End 2: Surface wear-recession made an originally-surface defect look "subsurface"
275	
276	**What was tried:** Explored whether gross material loss from ordinary abrasive/adhesive
277	boundary-lubrication wear could have receded the raceway surface enough that a defect which
278	actually originated at the (original) surface now measures as "0.4 mm below the surface" relative
279	to the new, worn-down surface — i.e., rescuing the operator's hypothesis by reinterpreting the
280	depth measurement rather than contesting it.
281	
282	**Why abandoned:** Two problems. First, 0.4 mm (400 µm) of uniform material loss from boundary
283	lubrication wear on a hardened raceway is itself a visually obvious, large-scale wear event that
284	would leave its own characteristic surface signature (dulling, scoring, measurable diameter loss)
285	distinct from — and in addition to — a crescent subsurface crack; none of that is reported. Second,
286	and decisively, this reinterpretation still does not explain GT-6's white-etching/butterfly
287	microstructure, which plain mechanical wear does not produce regardless of how the depth
288	measurement is framed. The hypothesis fails on the same ground truth that defeats Dead End 1.
289	
290	**What it ruled out:** Saves a reviewer from trying to rescue the operator's hypothesis by
291	arguing about the depth measurement's reference frame rather than its mechanism; chain C2 cites
292	this dead end as part of its own internal reasoning (it is the "artifact" alternative hop 4 rules
293	out).
294	
295	### Dead End 3: A single lightning-strike transient, rather than chronic converter-driven shaft voltage, is the electrical driver
296	
297	**What was tried:** Because this is an upwind turbine with direct lightning exposure through the
298	blades and drivetrain, considered whether a single large lightning-induced current transient
299	(rather than chronic low-level PWM-converter shaft voltage) was the electrical mechanism bearing
300	on C8.
301	
302	**Why abandoned:** A single discrete high-energy transient event is the wrong shape for this
303	failure's own timeline. GT-2's detection signal is a *step increase* in an impulsive vibration
304	statistic consistent with a gradually-growing crack network, and C1 establishes that the crack
305	network almost certainly predates detection by some incubation interval — a pattern more
306	consistent with a chronic, recurring low-level stressor (chronic shaft voltage, per GT-15) than
307	with one discrete overstress event. A single-event hypothesis is not contradicted by any ground
308	truth outright, but it is not cited on any other chain's head and offers no verification path this
309	analysis can name beyond what the shaft-current/insulation test (already proposed for C8) would
310	also catch, so it does not warrant a separate chain; it is retained here as a named, considered,
311	and set-aside possibility rather than silently dropped.
312	
313	**What it ruled out:** Saves a reviewer from treating "lightning" and "chronic shaft current" as
314	two separate electrical hypotheses needing two separate tests — the single shaft-current/
315	insulation-resistance test proposed under C8 and in section 6 discriminates a chronic electrical
316	pathway either way, and a one-off lightning event would in any case leave the same kind of
317	discharge-site evidence (or absence of it) that test is designed to find.
318	
319	## 6. Conclusion
320	
321	**Recommended approach:** Authorize the replacement bearing specification as a combined package rather than a single-lever fix: (a) a lubricant/moisture-control upgrade plus WEC-resistant bearing metallurgy or surface treatment addressing the verified hydrogen-assisted white-etching-crack mechanism, run in parallel with (b) a mandatory electrical-verification track — insulation-resistance testing and shaft-current monitoring across the grounding brush — before the investigation is closed, rather than adopting the operator's viscosity-only remedy as sufficient on its own (chain C11).
322	
323	**Key insight:** The L10 ratio alone (~11%) is not by itself anomalous, since a single early failure is statistically expected in any bearing population (chain C3) — but this failure's ratio lands inside the narrow 5–10%-of-rating-life band specifically documented for the white-etching-crack failure population, and it is only the combination of that narrow-band timing match with the subsurface white-etching microstructure, not either fact alone, that rules out both "ordinary bad luck" and "ordinary bad lubrication" as the explanation (chain C9).
324	
325	**Trade-offs acknowledged:** Committing to the combined package defers closing the investigation on the operator's cheaper, single-lever theory (oil grade/viscosity alone) until the electrical test clears, costing schedule time and some near-term spend; chain C10 shows the lubricant-chemistry and electrical candidates are both still live and separately testable, so authorizing only the mechanical/lubrication half of the package on the operator's original theory would leave a credible competing failure pathway (electrical) completely unaddressed (chain C10). Separately, this analysis has not independently re-audited the original L10 calculation's load-spectrum inputs; if that calculation itself understated the applied loads, the apparent prematurity would be smaller than the raw ~11% figure suggests, though this would not change the metallurgical case against the operator's literal wear-through hypothesis — no chain — flagged assumption only.
326	
327	**Confidence:** MEDIUM — capped by C6, C9, C10 and C11 (each MEDIUM); C6 and C9 are themselves capped by C2 and C4's unread primary WEC literature (GT-12?, GT-13?, GT-17?, GT-18?) and C10/C11 additionally by the unresolved electrical test (C8, GT-14?/GT-15?); no further Conclusion-level downgrade cause exists beyond what each cited chain's own confidence line already explains. The band would move to HIGH if (i) the primary WEC-mechanism literature underlying GT-12?/GT-13?/GT-17?/GT-18? were opened and confirmed at source, and (ii) the shaft-current/insulation-resistance test underlying C8 came back clean (ruling the electrical pathway out) or conclusively in (ruling it in and resolving C10's ranking).
328
